Rashi on Chullin 95b:10:1.hebrew: כולהו שני - דהוה רב קיים בבבל, כי הוה כתב ר' יוחנן מארץ ישראל שאלה או תשובה, היה כותב באגרתו: "לקדם רבינו שבבבל":
Rashi on Chullin 95b:10:1.english: All the years - [that] Rav was alive in Babylonia, when Rabbi Yochanan would write a question or a response from the Land of Israel, he would write in his letter: "To our Master who is in Babylonia":

Rashi on Chullin 95b:10:3.hebrew: לא ידיע לי מידי דרביה אנא - לא אוכל לחפש דבר שאהיה אני בקי בו, והוא לא שנאו, ואהיה רבו:
Rashi on Chullin 95b:10:3.english: Is there not known to me something in which I am his master? - [Can] I not seek out something in which I am expert, and [which] he has not learned, and [thus] I will be his master?

Rashi on Chullin 95b:11:2.hebrew: ספקי טריפתא - מיני ספק טרפות. ואני שמעתי שהן הנך ספקי עופות טמאים ד"אלו טריפות" (לעיל חולין דף סב:):
Rashi on Chullin 95b:11:2.english: Uncertainties [pertaining to] tereifot - Types of doubtful tereifot. And I have heard [that these are] those uncertainties [regarding] non-kosher birds [discussed in the chapter] Eilu Tereifot (above, Chullin 62b):

Rashi on Chullin 95b:13:1.english: A house, a child, and a wife - [If] he built a house, or a son was born to him, or he married a wife:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:13:2.hebrew: אע"פ שאין נחש - שאסור לנחש ולסמוך על הנחש:
Rashi on Chullin 95b:13:2.english: Even though there is no divination - [meaning] that it is forbidden to practice divination and to rely on divination:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:13:3.hebrew: יש סימן - סימנא בעלמא הוי מיהא, דאי מצלח בסחורה ראשונה אחר שבנה בית או שנולד התינוק או שנשא אשה, סימן הוא שהולך ומצליח; ואי לא, אל ירגיל לצאת יותר מדאי, שיש לחוש שלא יצליח:
Rashi on Chullin 95b:13:3.english: There is a sign - It is merely a sign, however, that if one succeeds in [his] first business transaction after he built a house, or after the child was born, or after he married a woman, it is a sign that he will continue to succeed; and if not, he should not accustom himself to go out [on business] too much, for there is reason to fear that he will not succeed:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:14:1.english: Three times - [Whether] it succeeded or did not succeed:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:14:2.hebrew: יוסף איננו ושמעון איננו - הרי שתים; אם את בנימין תקחו, מיד "עלי היו כולנה", ואין לך צרה שאינה עוברת עלי:
Rashi on Chullin 95b:14:2.english: Joseph is not, and Simeon is not - [that is] two; if you take Benjamin, immediately "all these things are upon me," and there is no trouble that does not pass over me:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:15:1.hebrew: בחרוזין מהו - נתן בשר בחרוזין, רישט"ש, ונתעלם מן העין:
Rashi on Chullin 95b:15:1.english: [If it is] strung together, what is [the law]? - [This means] he placed meat on strings — [in Old French:] restes — and it became obscured from sight:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:15:2.hebrew: אל תהי שוטה בחרוזים - בשאלה זו, דודאי זה סימן; לשון מורי. לישנא אחרינא: אל תהי שוטה, דבחרוזין הרי זה סימן:
Rashi on Chullin 95b:15:2.english: Do not be a fool regarding strung [pieces] - [meaning, do not be a fool] in this question, for certainly this is a distinguishing mark; [this is] the wording of my teacher. Another version: Do not be a fool, for [when they are] strung together it is a distinguishing mark:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:15:3.hebrew: איכא דאמרי - לאו בעיא הוא, אלא שמעתא אתמר: אמר רב הונא כו':
Rashi on Chullin 95b:15:3.english: There are [those] who say - It is not a question [that was asked], rather a teaching was stated: "Rav Huna said, etc."

Rashi on Chullin 95b:16:2.hebrew: האידנא דהיתרא שכיח טפי - דהיום רוב שוחטים ישראלים הם, ולספק טרפה לא חיישינן, דרוב בהמות אינן טרפות:
Rashi on Chullin 95b:16:2.english: At this time, when permitted [meat] is more common - For today most slaughterers are Jews, and we are not concerned about a possible terefah [an animal with a disqualifying defect], because most animals are not terefot:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:17:1.hebrew: כרכשא - טבחי"א: רב הונא ס"ל כרב רביה דאסר בהעלמה, ולא קי"ל כוותיה בהא, אלא אמתניתין סמכינן: "נמצא בגבולים, מצא בה בשר". ואע"ג דשנינהו בעומד ורואהו, שינויי דחיקי נינהו. וכי קי"ל "הלכתא כרב באיסורי", גבי פלוגתא דשמואל הוא דאמרינן, אבל גבי מתניתין לא. ורב כהנא, הא קא חזינן דא"ל: "שקול אכול":
Rashi on Chullin 95b:17:1.english: Karkasha - Tivchaya [a stuffed intestine]: Rav Huna holds like Rav, his teacher, who prohibits [meat] upon concealment [from sight]. However, we do not rule like him in this [matter]; rather, we rely on our Mishnah: "[If it was] found in the borders... [if] one found meat in it." And even though [the Gemara] resolved them as [referring to] one who is standing and watching it, they are forced resolutions. And when we establish that "the halakhah follows Rav in ritual prohibitions," it is regarding a dispute with Shmuel that we say [this], but against a Mishnah, [we do] not. And [as for] Rav Kahana, behold we see that he said to him, "Take [and] eat":

Rashi on Chullin 95b:19:1.english: A skein - [In Old French,] limoisel [a ball or skein of thread]:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:19:2.english: Tekhelet [sky-blue wool] - one must recognize it so that it not be confused with kala ilan [an imitation indigo dye]:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:1:1.english: Cleaning - Rinsing it and washing it in water:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:1:3.hebrew: עבדי נמי הכי - וכי דרך הוא כן שהמאבד חפץ אחד מוצא שנים? כלומר, אחרים הוו נמי התם ברישא:
Rashi on Chullin 95b:1:3.english: Does it also happen this way - Is it really usual that one who loses one object finds two? That is to say, other [heads] were also there originally:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:20:1.hebrew: דהא מהדרינן אבידתא - לכל אדם בסימנין, ולא מהדרינן אבידתא בטביעות עינא אלא לצורבא מרבנן, באלו מציאות (ב"מ דף כג:):
Rashi on Chullin 95b:20:1.english: Because we return a lost item - to any person based on distinguishing marks, and we do not return a lost item based on visual recognition except to a Torah scholar, [as stated] in [the chapter] Eilu Metzi'ot (Bava Metzia 23b):

Rashi on Chullin 95b:2:1.hebrew: דהיתירא לא שכיחי - בתמיה, האי נמי דהיתירא הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 95b:2:1.english: [Is] permitted [meat] not common - [This is said] as a rhetorical question: this [meat] too is permitted.

Rashi on Chullin 95b:3:1.hebrew: וכי מכללא מאי - לעיל קאי, דאמרי "לאו בפירוש איתמר": מאי בין פירושא לכללא? והא שפיר שמעינן מינה דכיון שנתעלם אסור, מדאסר לראש הנמצא. ומשני: איכא בינייהו דליכא למיסמך אמילתא כולי האי, דאיכא למימר ברוב טבחי ישראל מודה דמותר, והכא משום דפרוותא דעובדי כוכבים הואי — נמל, פור"ט — ושכיחי דאיסורא טפי:
Rashi on Chullin 95b:3:1.english: And if by inference, what [of it] - It refers to above, where they said, "it was not stated explicitly": What [difference is there] between an explicit statement and an inference? Surely we learn well from it that once [meat] disappears from sight it is forbidden, since [Rav] forbade the head that was found! And [the Gemara] answers: There is [a difference] between them in that one cannot rely on the matter to such an extent, for one can say [that] where the majority of butchers are Jewish [Rav] concedes that it is permitted, and here [he forbade it] because it was a *parvata* of gentiles — [meaning] a harbor, *port* [in Old French] — and forbidden [meat] is more common:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:4:1.english: But how did Rav eat meat - since he forbids it when [it is] out of sight:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:4:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: "In its time" - immediately when it was slaughtered:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:4:3.hebrew: אתלת קרנתא - לכל חתיכה ג' קרנות, ומשום סימן שלא יגנבו ממנה אנשי ביתו:
Rashi on Chullin 95b:4:3.english: Into three corners - Each piece [has] three corners, and [this was] as a distinguishing mark so that the members of his household would not steal from it:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:5:1.english: He saw a ferry - a river ferryboat that was coming from the other side to this side:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:5:2.hebrew: אמר מברא אתי לאפאי יומא טבא לגו - סימן טוב הוא לעוברי דרכים: כשהמעבורת באה לקראתן מאליה קודם שזימנוה, יום טוב להם בבית אושפיזם באותה לילה כשילינו:
Rashi on Chullin 95b:5:2.english: He said, "The ferry is coming toward me; [there is] a good day inside" - It is a good omen for travelers: when the ferry comes toward them on its own before they summoned it, [it indicates] a good day for them in the house of their host that night when they lodge [there]:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:6:1.english: He looked through a crack in the door - He peeked through a crack in the door:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:6:2.hebrew: איכו השתא - כלומר, אם בשמירתכם השתא:
Rashi on Chullin 95b:6:2.english: If now - That is to say, if [it depended on] your watching now:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:6:3.english: You would have fed forbidden [meat] to the sons of my daughter - [because] you averted your eyes [from the meat]:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:7:1.hebrew: דנחיש - אמעברא דאתא לאפיה, דאמר: "יומא טבא לגו":
Rashi on Chullin 95b:7:1.english: Because he divined - [This refers] to the ferry that came toward him, for he had said: "[There is] a good day inside."

Rashi on Chullin 95b:8:1.hebrew: כל נחש שאינו - סומך עליו ממש כאליעזר עבד אברהם, שאם תשקני, אדבר בה, ואם לאו, לא אדבר בה:
Rashi on Chullin 95b:8:1.english: Any divination that is not - [meaning, where one] relies upon it completely like Eliezer, the servant of Abraham, [who resolved] that if she gives me to drink, I will speak about her [for marriage], and if not, I will not speak about her:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:8:2.english: And like Jonathan, son of Saul - [Who said,] "If they say (come up to us), then we will go up":

Rashi on Chullin 95b:8:3.hebrew: סעודת הרשות - כגון בת ת"ח לע"ה, באלו עוברין (פסחים מט.):
Rashi on Chullin 95b:8:3.english: An optional feast - [such as the wedding of] the daughter of a Torah scholar to an ignoramus, [as taught in the chapter] Eilu Ovrin (Pesachim 49a):

Rashi on Chullin 95b:9:1.hebrew: בדיק במברא - אם מזומנת לו, אזיל, ואם בקושי מוצאה, לא אזיל:
Rashi on Chullin 95b:9:1.english: [Rav] would check by the ferry - If it was readily available to him, he would go; and if he found it [only] with difficulty, he would not go:

Rashi on Chullin 95b:9:2.english: By a child - [meaning] that he asks him, "Recite your verse to me":

Tosafot on Chullin 95b:11:1.hebrew: תריסר גמלי - ור"ח גריס גוילי, כלומר תריסר גוילין כתובין שאלות:
Tosafot on Chullin 95b:11:1.english: Twelve camels - And Rabbeinu Ḥananel reads "gevilei" [parchment scrolls], that is to say, twelve parchment scrolls written [with] questions:

Tosafot on Chullin 95b:15:1.hebrew: בחרוזים הרי זה סימן - משמע דאין דרך לחרוז בשר. וא"ת: דבתוספתא [ב"מ פ"ב] קתני "מצא חרוזין של דגים ושל בשר, הרי אלו שלו"? ויש לומר, דהכא סמכינן בדבר מועט:
Tosafot on Chullin 95b:15:1.english: Strung together, it is a distinguishing mark - This implies that it is not customary to string meat together. And if you say [in objection]: in the Tosefta [Bava Metzia, ch. 2] it teaches: "[If] one found strings of fish or of meat, these belong to him" [implying it is not a distinguishing mark]? One can say [in resolution] that here [regarding meat obscured from sight], we rely on [even] a slight [distinguishing mark]:

Tosafot on Chullin 95b:1:1.hebrew: אסיק תרין אמר רב עבדי נמי הכי אסרינהו ניהליה - ואי לא אסיק אלא חד, לא היה אוסר, שהרי ראה שלא היה שם עורב; והא לא הוה למיחש שמא שלו נאבד במים וזהו אחר. אבל השתא דאסיק תרי, אסרינן, אע"פ שרוב טבחי ישראל הוו שם, דחייש שמא עורב הביא מרובא דעלמא. והיינו דקאמר "דאיסורא שכיח טפי", כלומר: במקומות הרחוקים שיכולים עורבין להביא משם. ולקמן, דשרי רב כהנא כבדי וכולייתא דמייתו עורבין ושדו, משום דהיתרא שכיחא התם — בכל מקומות שסביב שהיו עורבין יכולים להביא משם, היו רוב טבחי ישראל:
Tosafot on Chullin 95b:1:1.english: He pulled out two; Rav said: Does it commonly happen this way? He rendered them forbidden to him - Had he pulled out only one, [Rav] would not have forbidden [it], because he saw that there was no raven there; and one would not have to be concerned that his [head] was lost in the water and this is another one. However, now that he pulled out two, we forbid [them], even though the majority of the butchers there were Jewish, because [Rav] is concerned that a raven brought [the second one] from the majority of the world. And this is what [Rav] meant when he said, "Forbidden [meat] is more common" — that is, in the distant places from which ravens are able to bring [meat]. And later, where Rav Kahana permits livers and kidneys that ravens bring and drop because permitted [meat] is common there — in all the surrounding places from which ravens were able to bring [meat], the majority of the butchers were Jewish:

Tosafot on Chullin 95b:6:1.hebrew: לא עלים רב עיניה מיניה - לא היה יכול לדקדק מכאן דסבר רב דבשר שנתעלם מן העין אסור, דדלמא רוב טבחי עובדי כוכבים היו שם:
Tosafot on Chullin 95b:6:1.english: Rav did not remove his eyes from it - One could not deduce from here that Rav holds that meat that was out of sight is forbidden, for perhaps the majority of butchers there were non-Jews:

Tosafot on Chullin 95b:8:1.hebrew: כאליעזר עבד אברהם - ואם תאמר: אליעזר היאך ניחש, למ"ד בפ' ארבעה מיתות (סנהדרין דף נו:) "כל האמור בפרשת מכשף בן נח מוזהר עליו"? וי"ל, דההוא תנא סבר שלא נתן לה הצמידים עד שהגידה לו בת מי היא; ואע"ג דכתיב (בראשית כד) "ויקח האיש נזם זהב וגו'", והדר כתיב "ויאמר בת מי את", אין מוקדם ומאוחר בתורה. וכן מוכח כשספר, דכתיב: "ואשאל אותה ואומר בת מי את":
Tosafot on Chullin 95b:8:1.english: Like Eliezer, the servant of Abraham - And if you ask: How could Eliezer practice divination, according to the one who says in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 56b), "Everything stated in the passage of the sorcerer, a Noahide is warned against [doing] it"? One can answer that that Tanna holds that he did not give her the bracelets until she told him whose daughter she was; and even though it is written (Genesis 24), "And the man took a gold nose-ring, etc.," and afterward it is written, "And he said: Whose daughter are you?" — there is no chronological order in the Torah. And so it is proven when he recounted [the story], as it is written: "And I asked her, and I said: Whose daughter are you?":

Tosafot on Chullin 95b:8:2.hebrew: וכיונתן בן שאול - וא"ת, היאך ניחש? ויש לומר, דלזרז את נערו אמר כן, ובלאו הכי נמי היה עולה:
Tosafot on Chullin 95b:8:2.english: And like Jonathan, son of Saul - And if you ask: How did he practice divination? One can say that he said this [only] to encourage his attendant, and even without this he would have gone up:
